remove: The ink-trap notches cut into every glyph. At 210 px cap height they read as chipped, broken corners rather than cut wood type, and they add noise to the one gesture. Keep the chamfers only.
top_problem: The boldest missing idea is the Iowa City half of the thesis, which exists only in proposal.md. On the page, the guest sees a black block CANTINA with an offset red drop shadow. That reads as a varsity-jersey or sports-sign cliché, not a two-plate press misregistration. It sits one step from ref-02 panel 4 (the vertical cropped CANTINA) and would pass the substitution test for any cantina anywhere. Brief section 5 asks for Mexico and Iowa City fused in the idea itself, and nothing a guest can see does that.
fixes: Make the press reading visible: print the chile plate as a true overprint (multiply, where red over black darkens and red shows on both sides of the stroke, not only on the top and left edges), or slip it along the letter axis so it cannot read as a drop shadow.

Carry the Mexico and Iowa City fusion into something a guest sees without adding a label or tagline, for example rótulo sombra construction plus a wood-type edge or letterpress deboss, so the gesture fails the substitution test.
Drop names to about 14 pt and descriptions to about 10 pt on one shared baseline grid across both columns, so the reading layer goes quiet as in ref-02 and rows align column to column.
Rebreak the cocktail descriptions so ingredients never split ('lime wheel' and 'cocktail cherry' stay whole) and no line holds a single word.
Make the sub-head level consistent: either stack 'Draft' as its own sub-head row like Classics and Agave, or drop it (every beer description already says draft or lager).

lens: Items and prices against draft_doc.json rev 3; how complete the ingredients and descriptions are (public_components honoured); section flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The cocktails are well built from sourced components, but everything else is thin. Beer has no ABV. Wine has no region, and Brut Rosé has no grape. The spirits have no producer, brand or house pour. Three descriptions just repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour'), and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' repeats 'IPA'. None of these gaps is flagged missing_ingredients in proposal.md; the source column calls them 'draft desc, full'. That leaves 9 of 14 items reading as placeholders.
problems: Prices: all 14 match the draft exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Dry Cider 8). No item was invented or dropped. Format is one style: whole numbers, no $, inline. The price sits on the name's last line with short eye travel, so both gates pass.

Hidden component handled correctly: Manhattan leaves out Aromatic Bitters (public_components aromatic-bitters:false). Brown Butter Old Fashioned (house_recipe:false) shows names without quantities. Garnishes are said to come from recipe_versions (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel); the accuracy reviewer should verify them.

Criterion 8: beer has style only, no ABV. Malbec and Pinot Grigio have a grape but no region. Brut Rosé has neither grape nor region. Blanco and Añejo Tequila have no producer or agave source. Cognac VSOP has no house. None is flagged missing_ingredients, which the scorecard requires.

Description voice is split three ways: dot-separated ingredient lists for cocktails, the full sentence 'Bright and citrus-forward.' tacked onto the Margarita alone, and bare three-word category phrases for everything else. It reads like three data sources, not one editor (criterion 10).

Flow: section order changed from the draft (Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider) to Cocktails, Beer, Spirits, Wine, Cider. The reason given is column balance, not guest logic. Cider is stranded at the bottom of the right column, far from Beer, its natural neighbour. Wine lands mid-column after a stretched gap.

Criterion 5: the per-column fill sets a different item rhythm in each section and column. Beer rows are much looser than the cocktail rows above them. There are large dead bands between Cognac VSOP and WINE, between Brut Rosé and CIDER, and between the Old Fashioned and BEER. These read as holes, not grouping. The right column's SPIRITS head also competes with COCKTAILS as a second entry point at the same height.
Letter description breaks leave widows: 'lime / wheel' (Margarita), 'cocktail / cherry' (Manhattan), 'demerara / syrup' (Daiquiri). Each splits a two-word ingredient across lines.

CANTINA plus '& Cocktail Bar / Iowa City, Iowa' is printed as the venue name, but the draft title is 'Bar menu' and the draft has no venue name. It states no item fact, so the tagline rule passes. The Coordinator should still confirm the venue is actually named or known as 'Cantina' before print.
For a Mexican cantina, agave has only two items and the section heads are all English. That is data-bound, not invented, so it is noted but not penalised beyond flow.
fixes: Flag missing_ingredients for every non-cocktail item and ask for the facts: beer ABV and brewery; wine region, and grape for Brut Rosé; producer or house for Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP. Then rewrite the descriptions so none repeats the item name.

Restore guest-logical flow: move Cider directly under Beer (Beer / Cider in the left column), and use Cocktails, Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits, or lead the right column with Agave if the venue wants agave emphasis, stating why. Rebalance the columns with type size, not stretched gaps.
Replace the per-column fitted unit with one shared item rhythm and one shared section gap across both columns, so the Beer rows match the Cocktail rows and the holes above WINE, CIDER and BEER close.
Pick one description voice. Either every cocktail gets a short flavour line after its ingredient list, or the Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' moves into the same dot-list grammar.
Keep multi-word ingredients together (non-breaking spaces in 'lime wheel', 'cocktail cherry', 'demerara syrup', 'agave syrup') so no ingredient is split across a line break on letter or phone.

lens: Traced every printed ingredient, garnish and label to build/draft_doc.json (rev 3) and phg.recipe_versions (gateway log_id 217), and checked how descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png
top_problem: Every fact traces to a source, but half the menu has no real description. 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour' and 'VSOP Cognac pour' only repeat the item name. 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Crisp pale lager' and 'Dry sparkling cider' read like category labels, not guest language. A Mexican cantina's agave list has two lines and no Spanish voice beyond the drawn CANTINA, so the whole list below the cocktails could belong to any bar. Verified sources: prices 15/15/14/16/7/8/7/12/16/18/12/11/13/8 match the menu_items.menu_price rows and draft_doc prices. Garnishes trace to recipe_versions.garnish: Margarita f06abb74 'Lime wheel', Manhattan 9fb77eaa 'Cocktail cherry', House Daiquiri 14d45e57 'Lime coin', Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d 'Orange peel'. Components trace to the draft_doc components: Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup, Rye Whiskey, Sweet Vermouth, White Rum, Demerara Syrup, Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Aromatic Bitters. Leaving Aromatic Bitters off the Manhattan correctly follows meta.public_components.aromatic-bitters=false. 'Bright and citrus-forward.' is the draft Margarita desc. The beer, wine, spirits and cider descriptions are the draft/menu_items menu_description verbatim, with the periods dropped. Accents match the source (Añejo, Brut Rosé). No tagline states an item fact. 'Junmai Ginjo' is a menu_items row that is absent from draft rev 3 and correctly not printed. Prices sit inline about 0.9 em after the name on the same line, so there is no association risk.
fixes: Criterion 12: the three spirits descriptions only repeat their names. Replace them with sourced facts (agave type, age statement, producer from spirit_lexicon / brands / products); where no row exists, flag missing_ingredients instead of printing a name echo.

Criteria 12/13: the wine lines have no grape region or producer, the beers have no style or ABV, and the cider has no producer, so the content does not meet the scorecard's own minimum for these categories. Request those rows (brands / products / beverage_categories), or flag missing_ingredients in proposal.md, rather than shipping 'Dry red wine' and 'Crisp pale lager'.

Criterion 14 (layout note for the designer): 'wheel' sits alone on the Margarita's third line, 'cherry' is orphaned on the Manhattan, and the Margarita is the only item with a second style sentence, which breaks the one-voice list. Rebalance the measure or break before the garnish so no line holds a single word, and either drop the style sentence or give every cocktail an equivalent line from sourced data.

Criterion 14: Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Sparkling' with no pour label. The glass reading is only implied by the earlier 'By the Glass' head, so a guest can read 13 as a bottle price. Confirm the pour in the draft and label it (for example 'Sparkling · by the glass'), or move it under By the Glass.

Criterion 13: for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, give the agave list real presence (the draft has only Blanco and Añejo). Keep 'Tequila blanco' and 'Blanco Tequila' in one word order across the menu, and add correct Spanish kickers only where they are sourced. Never invent regional or producer claims to fill the gap.
